description: Show today's routines and their completion status

system_context.engine_import: from engine.base import SkillBase, SkillRequest, SkillResponse

context.table_schema:
Table: routines
Columns:
  - id (integer, PK)
  - title (text, NOT NULL) -- the routine name, e.g. 'Check calendar'
  - description (text)
  - frequency (varchar(20), default 'daily') -- values: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'
  - day_of_week (integer) -- 0=Mon through 6=Sun, for weekly routines
  - day_of_month (integer) -- for monthly routines
  - time_due (time) -- when it should be done by
  - domain (varchar(50), default 'personal')
  - priority (varchar(20), default 'medium')
  - assigned_to (varchar(50), default 'adge')
  - is_active (boolean, default true)
  - sort_order (integer, default 100)

Table: routine_completions
Columns:
  - id (integer, PK)
  - routine_id (integer, FK to routines.id)
  - due_date (date, NOT NULL)
  - status (varchar(20), default 'pending') -- values: 'pending', 'completed', 'skipped'
  - completed_at (timestamp)
  - completed_by (varchar(50))
  - notes (text)
  UNIQUE on (routine_id, due_date)

NOTE: Column is 'title' NOT 'name'. Use routines.title for the routine name.

build_plan.instruction: Write file skeleton. Imports: os, logging, datetime (date, datetime), psycopg2, RealDictCursor, dotenv, engine.base. _get_conn() EXACTLY as mandatory_patterns. Class with all attributes. Methods have 'pass'. ASCII only.

Implement _query_routines_today(). Use _get_conn(). Get today = date.today(). Get day_of_week = today.weekday() (0=Monday). Get day_of_month = today.day. Query:

SELECT r.id, r.title, r.description, r.frequency, r.time_due, r.domain, r.priority, r.sort_order,
       rc.status as completion_status, rc.completed_at
FROM routines r
LEFT JOIN routine_completions rc ON rc.routine_id = r.id AND rc.due_date = %s
WHERE r.is_active = true
  AND (
    r.frequency = 'daily'
    OR (r.frequency = 'weekly' AND r.day_of_week = %s)
    OR (r.frequency = 'monthly' AND r.day_of_month = %s)
  )
ORDER BY r.sort_order, r.title

Params: (today, day_of_week, day_of_month). CRITICAL: use r.title NOT r.name. try/finally close.

Implement _format_results() and _build_summary(). Format: dict with id, title, frequency, time_due (str or None), domain, priority, is_complete (boolean: true if completion_status == 'completed'), completed_at (ISO str or None). Summary: count completed vs total. 'Routines: N of M complete.' If any done: 'Done: title1, title2.' If any remaining: 'Still to do: title3, title4.' If all done: 'All routines complete for today!'
